headline: Computational methods resolve which proteoform or isoform a peptide reflects
label: Computational Proteoform Identity Resolution
summary: Open-search and probabilistic frameworks are now applied to peptide-to-proteoform ambiguity, from AD brain proteomics to top-down detectability planning.
synthesis: The dominant thread is computational handling of ambiguity in protein identity: which proteoform or isoform a peptide reflects, and whether a workflow can resolve it. PIPI-C open-search analysis of two Alzheimer's disease proteomic datasets (AMP-AD, PXD013753) maps proteome-level amino acid substitutions, with N>M reported as most frequent. ProteoformTracker models MS1 and MS2 signal to judge whether top-down or middle-down proteomics can distinguish a target proteoform. A Bayesian method integrates peptidome and transcriptome data to estimate isoform abundances under ambiguous peptide mapping, with explicit uncertainty. Other items, including stability selection for DIA biomarker panels and LLM-based lipidomics workflows, emphasize analytical rigor over proteoform identity. What is new is the emphasis on open-search and probabilistic frameworks that model ambiguity in peptide-to-proteoform assignment.
